identity.title: Learning to grok: Emergence of in-context learning and skill composition in modular arithmetic tasks

problem.claim: Study how in-context learning and skill composition emerge in modular arithmetic tasks.

contributions.claim: Defines a finite family of linear modular functions, using some for pre-training and the remainder for out-of-distribution testing.
Reports a transition from in-distribution to out-of-distribution generalization as the number of pre-training tasks increases, with depth-dependent behavior.
Examines structured representations in attention heads and MLPs and discusses the learned algorithms.

stated_novelty.claim: The work studies the emergence of in-context learning and skill composition through a modular-arithmetic task collection, including an interpretability analysis of learned algorithms.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that the smallest model showing out-of-distribution generalization has two transformer blocks.
The authors report that out-of-distribution generalization is transient in deeper models, so early stopping is necessary.
The authors report an algorithmic shift in deeper models as the number of in-context examples grows from few to many.

narrative_sequence.summary: Frames unseen-task solving as associated with in-context learning and skill composition.
Studies a finite family of labeled linear modular functions, splitting tasks between pre-training and out-of-distribution testing.
Reports increasing-task-driven transition to out-of-distribution generalization and identifies different depth requirements and transient behavior.
Reports structured attention-head and MLP representations, learned algorithms, and an example-count-dependent algorithmic shift in deeper models.

source_observation.claim: The abstract links generalization behavior to both model depth and the number of pre-training tasks, and separately reports a shift with the number of in-context examples.

lessons.interpretation: Generalization may depend on training scale and inference-context regime in interacting, non-monotonic ways.
lessons.application: When presenting a generalization study, stratify results by model depth, training-task coverage, and context-example count, and state whether observed phases are transient.
lessons.exception: This framing may be unsuitable when the task or model has no meaningful notion of task coverage, depth, or in-context examples.

unknowns: The abstract does not provide quantitative transition points, model sizes beyond block depth, task-sampling details, or evaluation metrics.
The conditions and evidence supporting the claim that early stopping is necessary are not specified.
The interpretability findings and proposed learned algorithms are not described in enough detail to assess their exact mechanisms.
